newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

* Kenneth Starr, the special prosecutor investigating the Clintons' Whitewater land dealings, will step down from his post by August to become dean of the law and public policy schools at California's Pepperdine University.

* Pressure from Congress and Defense Department officials has prompted the Air Force to consider reversing its decision to exonerate Brig. Gen. Terryl Schwalier, who was in charge of the housing complex in Saudi Arabia where 19 American airmen were killed by a truck bomb.

* Instead of financing Republican senatorial campaigns, some donations to the National Republican Senatorial Committee, headed by Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, have ended up in the campaign war chest of New York Governor George Pataki.

* Federal regulators have decided to pay 41 of New York's teaching hospitals $400 million to not train so many new doctors in a plan called the Medicare Graduate Medical Education Demonstration Project.

* Jeanie Mentavlos, one of four female cadets admitted to the Citadel after the North Carolina school changed its all-male admissions policy, said in an interview that she was subjected to brutal hazing while at the school.

* A tabloid's decision to publish the names of five white youths accused of stabbing to death a black student -- even though the youths were not named in a guilty verdict after the case was reopened -- stirs debate in Britain.
* News Analysis: The defection of a high-ranking North Korean official and the shooting of another North Korean defector could deepen the friction between South Korea and the United States.
